t:
Section 1417 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3152) is amended—
    (1) in the matter preceding paragraph (1) of subsection (b), by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “land-grant colleges and universities”; and 
    (2) in subsection (d)(2), by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “universities”.

fable.w: This is a technical amendment that adds the University of the District of Columbia to the institutions covered by an existing agricultural education provision, which appears to concern grant eligibility. The tempting reading is that naming a non-federal university brings an outside party into a federal decision, but the text creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Eligibility for grants or benefits is not participation under the definition.
fable.s: by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “land-grant colleges and universities”

opus.w: This amendment only adds the University of the District of Columbia to the institutions covered by Section 1417, which deals with higher-education grants, so it is about grant eligibility. Naming an outside university is tempting, but applying for or being eligible for grants is not participation under the definition. The text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “land-grant colleges and universities”
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading.** The amendment names an outside institution, the University of the District of Columbia, in a federal program. That might look like bringing a non-federal party into federal activity. It fails the definition because the change only adds the university to the "land-grant colleges and universities" covered by Section 1417 (7 U.S.C. 3152), which deals with higher-education grants. Being eligible for grants is not participation. The text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to include the University of the District of Columbia in lists of eligible institutions. It does not require the federal government to consult with the university or any other outside party before making a decision. It merely changes eligibility criteria, which is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1417 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3152) is amended— (1) in the matter preceding paragraph (1) of subsection (b), by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “land-grant colleges and universities”; and (2) in subsection (d)(2), by inserting “(including the University of the District of Columbia)” after “universities”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that adding the University of the District of Columbia to a list of eligible entities implies some form of consultation or participation process. However, this is merely an amendment to eligibility criteria for funding or program inclusion, not a requirement for the government to consult with outsiders before making a decision. The text does not describe a process where the government seeks input from the university or other external parties; it simply expands the definition of who can receive benefits or be included in a program. This falls under the "No" category for applications for benefits or grants, or simply administrative definitions, rather than participation in decision-making.
